topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the course context, and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Processes vs. Environmental Exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual framework of cancer development by exploring the balance between intrinsic genetic and endogenous mutational processes versus environmental exposures and epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms of Carcinogens and Tumor Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific infectious, dietary, and chemical agents to explain their mechanisms of DNA damage, metabolic activation, tissue and developmental specificity, and promotion of tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Experimental and Epidemiological Methods for Assessing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic sequencing, biobanking, animal testing, and in vitro assay methods used to identify mutational signatures and prove carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic synthesizes the key themes of the lecture and frames cancer causation within everyday risk-benefit decision-making.
